families.scope: A pre-registered, frozen-decision-rule adversarial audit of six prior generative-falsification family claims: (1) discovery and quantification that the shared corpus parser used by prior pilots leaves IVTFF markup inside ~24% of published types, requiring restatement of all headline manuscript metrics under a newly implemented clean parser (with two uncertain-space treatment variants); (2) an alphabet-confound test showing the H2|1 anomaly is robust to EVA multigraph/determinism-merge alphabet normalization but the final-glyph anomaly is alphabet-dependent (0.08-0.27 bit gap depending on glyph-identity assumptions); (3) five untuned cipher constructions applied to real Latin/Culpeper plaintexts, showing a plain verbose cipher of Latin reproduces both entropy residues and fails only a type-ratio gate calibrated to the contaminated parser count; (4) permutation-null and Currier-language/section confound analysis showing the 'neighbouring-page 2x sharing' and '30% page-private' structural claims are largely artefacts of language/section confounding and hapax richness; (5) a new medieval-orthography control (two Chaucer editions) testing whether the vocabulary-richness anomaly survives non-standardized spelling.

families.scope: A bounded diagnostic control extending the generative-falsification metric suite (final-glyph entropy, conditional bigram entropy H2|1, type/token diversity, word length) to nine same-text (Bible) translations at equal 35k-token samples, testing whether a morphologically rich real language naturally reproduces the manuscript's word-ending discipline. Finds no tested language reaches the manuscript on either final-glyph entropy or H2|1; Finnish is nearest on endings (2.80 vs 2.58) but not close on H2|1; Russian, despite rich inflection, has the least predictable endings, refuting a simple morphology-based explanation; manuscript retains highest type diversity of all ten texts.
